title: AP Special TET Physical Science — Content & Pedagogy Batch 02

questions.question: The SI unit of pressure is:
questions.explanation: Pressure is measured in pascals (Pa), equivalent to N/m².

questions.question: A body covers 120 m in 20 s. Its average speed is:
questions.explanation: Average speed = distance ÷ time = 120 ÷ 20 = 6 m/s.

questions.question: A velocity-time graph has a horizontal line above the time axis. The body is moving with:
questions.explanation: A constant positive velocity is represented by a horizontal line above the time axis.

questions.question: The slope of a distance-time graph represents:
questions.explanation: The slope gives change in distance per unit time, i.e. speed.

questions.question: A force of 20 N acts on a 5 kg body. Acceleration is:
questions.explanation: Newton's second law gives a = F/m = 20/5 = 4 m/s².

questions.question: Momentum is the product of:
questions.explanation: Linear momentum is p = mv.

questions.question: The SI unit of momentum is:
questions.explanation: Momentum has units kg·m/s.

questions.question: Action and reaction forces act on:
options: The same body in the same direction
Different bodies in the same direction
questions.explanation: Newton's third-law force pair acts on two interacting bodies in opposite directions.

questions.question: A 2 kg object moves at 3 m/s. Its kinetic energy is:
questions.explanation: KE = ½mv² = ½ × 2 × 9 = 9 J.

questions.question: A 10 N force moves an object 4 m in its direction. Work done is:
questions.explanation: Work = force × displacement = 10 × 4 = 40 J.

questions.question: If 600 J of work is done in 30 s, power is:
questions.explanation: Power = work/time = 600/30 = 20 W.

questions.question: The energy stored in food is primarily:
questions.explanation: Food stores chemical potential energy.

questions.question: The law of conservation of energy states that energy:
options: Changes form but total energy is conserved
questions.explanation: Energy transfers and transforms; it is not created or destroyed.

questions.question: The value of acceleration due to gravity near Earth's surface is approximately:
questions.explanation: Near Earth's surface, g is about 9.8 m/s².

questions.question: The weight of a 4 kg mass on Earth (g ≈ 10 m/s²) is:
questions.explanation: Weight = mg = 4 × 10 = 40 N.

questions.question: An object's mass on the Moon compared with Earth is:
questions.explanation: Mass is intrinsic and does not change with location.

questions.question: The buoyant force on an immersed object equals the weight of:
questions.explanation: Archimedes' principle states that upthrust equals the weight of displaced fluid.

questions.question: A hydrometer is used to compare:
questions.explanation: A hydrometer measures liquid density or specific gravity.

questions.question: The density of a 200 g object with volume 50 cm³ is:
questions.explanation: Density = mass/volume = 200/50 = 4 g/cm³.

questions.question: Why does a sharp knife cut more easily than a blunt one?
options: It produces greater pressure for the same force
It reduces the applied force to zero
questions.explanation: A smaller contact area produces greater pressure for a given force.

questions.question: The phenomenon responsible for a straw appearing bent in water is:
questions.explanation: Light changes direction as it passes between media, causing refraction.

questions.question: A ray travelling from air into glass bends:
options: Without changing direction in all cases
questions.explanation: On entering a higher refractive-index medium obliquely, light bends towards the normal.

questions.question: The refractive index of a medium is the ratio of:
options: Speed in medium to speed in vacuum
Speed in vacuum to speed in medium
questions.explanation: Absolute refractive index n = c/v.

questions.question: A concave mirror can form a real, inverted image when the object is:
questions.explanation: For an object beyond the focal point, a concave mirror forms a real, inverted image.

questions.question: A convex mirror is commonly used as a vehicle rear-view mirror because it:
options: Provides a wide field of view
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors provide a wide field of view and form virtual, erect, diminished images.

questions.question: The splitting of white light into its component colours is:
questions.explanation: Dispersion separates colours because refractive index varies with wavelength.

questions.question: A rainbow is produced mainly by refraction, dispersion and:
questions.explanation: Water droplets refract and disperse sunlight and internally reflect it.

questions.question: The image formed on the retina is:
questions.explanation: The eye lens forms a real, inverted image on the retina; the brain interprets it.

questions.question: Myopia is commonly corrected using a:
questions.explanation: A concave lens diverges incoming light to help focus distant images on the retina.

questions.question: The unit of frequency is:
questions.explanation: Frequency is measured in hertz (Hz), or cycles per second.

questions.question: If a wave has frequency 50 Hz and wavelength 4 m, its speed is:
questions.explanation: Wave speed v = fλ = 50 × 4 = 200 m/s.

questions.question: An echo is heard due to:
questions.explanation: An echo is reflected sound heard after a delay.

questions.question: Ultrasound has a frequency:
questions.explanation: Ultrasound frequencies exceed the approximate upper human hearing limit of 20 kHz.

questions.question: Sound travels fastest, in general, through:
questions.explanation: Sound usually travels fastest in solids because particles are strongly coupled.

questions.question: The time period of a 5 Hz vibration is:
questions.explanation: Time period T = 1/f = 1/5 = 0.2 s.

questions.question: A tuning fork produces sound due to:
questions.explanation: A tuning fork's vibrating prongs set the surrounding air into vibration.

questions.question: The Celsius temperature corresponding to 300 K is approximately:
questions.explanation: °C = K − 273.15, so 300 K is about 27°C.

questions.question: Heat required to raise 2 kg of water by 5°C (c = 4200 J/kg°C) is:
The transfer of heat by bulk movement of fluid is:
questions.explanation: Convection transfers heat through movement of a fluid.

questions.question: A thermos flask reduces heat transfer by using:
questions.explanation: Vacuum reduces conduction and convection; reflective surfaces reduce radiation.

questions.question: The change from gas to liquid is called:
questions.explanation: Condensation is the transition from gas to liquid.

questions.question: Latent heat is energy absorbed or released during:
options: A change of state without temperature change
questions.explanation: Latent heat is associated with phase change at constant temperature.

questions.question: Which is a chemical property of a substance?
questions.explanation: Flammability describes a substance's ability to undergo combustion.

questions.question: An element consists of:
options: A physically mixed set of substances
questions.explanation: An element is made of atoms with the same atomic number.

questions.question: A compound differs from a mixture because a compound has:
options: Components chemically combined in a fixed ratio
Components that retain all original properties
questions.explanation: Compounds have chemically bonded elements in definite proportions.

questions.question: Which method separates miscible liquids with different boiling points?
questions.explanation: Fractional distillation separates miscible liquids based on boiling-point differences.

questions.question: Chromatography is particularly useful for separating:
options: Iron from sulphur with a magnet
Oil from water using a funnel only
questions.explanation: Chromatography separates mixture components through differing movement between phases.

questions.question: The atomic number of an atom equals the number of:
questions.explanation: Atomic number is the number of protons in the nucleus.

questions.question: Isotopes of an element have the same number of:
questions.explanation: Isotopes share proton number but differ in neutron number.

questions.question: An ion forms when an atom:
options: Changes its proton count in ordinary chemical reactions
Changes into a different isotope only
Splits its nucleus in every case
questions.explanation: Electron gain or loss gives an atom a net electrical charge.

questions.question: A solution with pH 9 is:
questions.explanation: A pH above 7 is basic (alkaline) in the usual aqueous scale.

questions.question: When an acid reacts with a base, the typical products are:
questions.explanation: Neutralization typically produces salt and water.

questions.question: Phenolphthalein in an alkaline solution is usually:
questions.explanation: Phenolphthalein turns pink in alkaline conditions.

questions.question: Which is an example of oxidation in everyday life?
questions.explanation: Rusting involves oxidation of iron.

questions.question: A catalyst changes the rate of a reaction by:
options: Being permanently consumed as a reactant
Providing an alternative pathway with different activation energy
Changing the products into elements always
questions.explanation: A catalyst offers an alternative pathway and is regenerated overall.

questions.question: Increasing temperature often increases reaction rate because particles:
questions.explanation: Higher temperature raises particle kinetic energy and the fraction of effective collisions.

questions.question: Which gas turns moist red litmus paper blue?
questions.explanation: Ammonia is alkaline in moist conditions and turns red litmus blue.

questions.question: The chief component of natural gas is usually:
questions.explanation: Natural gas consists predominantly of methane, though composition varies.

questions.question: Which allotrope of carbon conducts electricity well?
questions.explanation: Graphite has delocalized electrons that can carry electrical charge.

questions.question: The chemical formula of baking soda is:
questions.explanation: Baking soda is sodium hydrogen carbonate, NaHCO₃.

questions.question: The formula of quicklime is:
questions.explanation: Quicklime is calcium oxide, CaO.

questions.question: Which gas is commonly used in fire extinguishers because it does not support combustion?
questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide can displace oxygen around a fire and is non-combustible.

questions.question: The ozone layer absorbs much of the Sun's:
questions.explanation: Stratospheric ozone absorbs much of the harmful UV radiation.

questions.question: The major greenhouse gas emitted by burning fossil fuels is:
questions.explanation: Combustion of carbon-based fuels releases carbon dioxide.

questions.question: Which is a fossil fuel?
questions.explanation: Coal forms from ancient organic matter over geological time.

questions.question: The main function of a transformer is to change:
questions.explanation: A transformer steps AC voltage up or down through electromagnetic induction.

questions.question: A transformer works on the principle of:
questions.explanation: Changing current in the primary coil induces voltage in the secondary coil.

questions.question: The direction of induced current is described by:
questions.explanation: Lenz's law states the induced current opposes the change producing it.

questions.question: Ohm's law is expressed as:
questions.explanation: For an ohmic conductor under constant physical conditions, V = IR.

questions.question: A 12 V source across a 4 Ω resistor produces current:
An appliance draws 2 A from a 230 V supply. Its power is:
A 1 kW heater operates for 3 hours. Energy consumed is:
questions.explanation: Energy = power × time = 1 kW × 3 h = 3 kWh.

questions.question: The heating effect of current is the basis of an:
questions.explanation: An electric iron uses resistive heating to produce heat.

questions.question: The magnetic field around a straight current-carrying wire forms:
questions.explanation: The field lines are concentric circles around the wire.

questions.question: The core of a common electromagnet is often made of:
questions.explanation: Soft iron magnetizes readily and loses much of its magnetism when current stops.

questions.question: An electric bell uses:
options: Only a permanent magnet with no circuit
questions.explanation: Current energizes an electromagnet, repeatedly attracting the armature and interrupting the circuit.

questions.question: The SI unit of magnetic flux is:
questions.explanation: Magnetic flux is measured in webers (Wb).

questions.question: A solar cell converts light energy into:
options: Chemical fuel directly in all cases
questions.explanation: Photovoltaic cells convert incident light into electrical energy.

questions.question: Which is a semiconductor commonly used in electronic devices?
questions.explanation: Silicon is a widely used semiconductor material.

questions.question: A diode ideally allows current to flow mainly:
questions.explanation: A diode conducts primarily in its forward direction.

questions.question: A series connection of cells generally increases the:
options: Resistance of each cell to zero
questions.explanation: Cell voltages add in series when connected with matching polarity.

questions.question: A short circuit can cause dangerous heating because it creates:
options: A very low-resistance path and excessive current
questions.explanation: A low-resistance path can draw excessive current and overheat conductors.

questions.question: Which is the safest response to a person receiving an electric shock?
options: Touch them immediately with bare hands
Disconnect the power if safe and call for emergency help
Pull the person using a metal rod
questions.explanation: Cut power safely first; avoid direct contact while the person may remain energized.

questions.question: A student tests whether wire length affects resistance. Which variable should be kept constant?
questions.explanation: Keeping material and cross-sectional area fixed helps isolate length's effect.

questions.question: Which sequence best supports inquiry-based learning?
options: Question, predict, investigate, record, interpret, communicate
questions.explanation: The sequence gives learners an evidence-based process for investigating questions.

questions.question: In a science experiment, a control setup is used to:
options: Provide a comparison for interpreting the effect of a variable
questions.explanation: A control provides a baseline against which the experimental condition can be compared.

questions.question: A learner's claim is not supported by their data. The teacher should encourage them to:
options: Revise the claim or collect further evidence
Change recorded data to fit the claim
questions.explanation: Scientific claims should be aligned with evidence, and further testing may be warranted.

questions.question: Which assessment best checks a learner's ability to use a measuring cylinder correctly?
options: Observe the learner measure a liquid and read the meniscus
Ask for a definition of mass
Ask the learner to name a planet
questions.explanation: Direct performance observation checks the practical skill.

questions.question: Why should learners read a liquid meniscus at eye level?
questions.explanation: Eye-level reading helps avoid parallax and improves measurement accuracy.

questions.question: A teacher asks students to explain why an experiment may not establish causation. This develops:
questions.explanation: Evaluating causal claims requires considering design, confounding variables and evidence.

questions.question: Which is an appropriate adaptation for a learner with low vision during practical work?
options: Provide enlarged/high-contrast instructions and accessible equipment where possible
Exclude the learner from all experiments
questions.explanation: Accessible formats and equipment can support safe and meaningful participation.

questions.question: A learner gives an answer based on a misconception. An effective response is to:
options: Use a probing question or demonstration to examine the idea
questions.explanation: Probing and evidence-based discussion help uncover and address misconceptions.

questions.question: A teacher uses concept cartoons showing competing explanations of a phenomenon. They are useful for:
questions.explanation: Contrasting viewpoints can stimulate reasoning and expose prior conceptions.

questions.question: Which task best assesses application rather than recall?
options: Use heat-transfer principles to recommend insulation for a lunch container
questions.explanation: Applying principles to a design context requires transfer and decision-making.

questions.question: A learner notices an unexpected pattern and proposes a new test. This demonstrates:
options: An invalid action in all investigations
questions.explanation: Noticing patterns and proposing tests are core inquiry practices.

questions.question: Which classroom approach is most likely to support durable understanding?
options: Connect demonstrations, models, discussion and explanation
questions.explanation: Multiple connected representations and active explanation support conceptual learning.

questions.question: Why is it important to distinguish a scientific model from the real system?
options: A model simplifies selected features and has limitations
A model always includes every detail
A model is identical to direct observation
questions.explanation: Models are selective representations and should be evaluated for scope and limitations.

questions.question: A teacher asks students to communicate results with a labelled table and graph. This develops:
questions.explanation: Tables and graphs help communicate measured evidence clearly.

questions.question: Which statement best describes a theory in science?
options: A well-supported explanatory framework that accounts for evidence
A random guess with no testing
A fact that cannot be revised under any circumstances
questions.explanation: Scientific theories are comprehensive explanations supported by multiple lines of evidence.

questions.question: Which is a key feature of formative feedback?
options: It is timely and helps the learner improve
It is given only after the course ends
It contains a grade without guidance
questions.explanation: Timely, specific feedback helps learners identify progress and next steps.
